title: Create Google Calendar events with AI from a message
h1: put a new event in google calendar by asking
description: Turn a message into a timed or all-day Google Calendar event. Choose the calendar, time zone, guests and meeting link before the bot adds it.
keyword: google calendar create event with ai
answer: **get the appointment out of your messages and onto the calendar.** give a bot the title, date, time zone and duration. it can create timed or all-day entries. ask for availability separately. google emails all guests by default; dusk treats creation as a change. put review and notification choices in your request before the bot creates it.
og_line: a new appointment, with the details checked.
what:
**book the slot you agreed, on the calendar you meant.** choose your primary calendar, or ask the bot to list your calendars. look up availability separately before booking.

- timed entries need a start and an end or duration
- all-day entries end on the following date for a single day
- eligible events request a meet link by default; turn it off for a simple reminder
uses: **keep confirmed exhibition dates visible.** add an all-day entry.
**reserve the workshop slot.** include the street address and duration.
**stop losing repair appointments.** give the bot the date and time you agreed.
**keep practice at the right hour.** give repeating sessions an explicit time zone.

routine.message: each saturday at 10, read new emails from larch quay gallery in gmail from the past week. find confirmed exhibition dates, not tentative ones. compare them with my personal google calendar and skip entries already there. propose each missing all-day event with its venue. ask me before creating anything. add only approved events, with no guests, no meeting link and guest notifications off. list the saved entries here. never change existing events.
routine.needs: gmail connected as read only; google calendar connected with read and write for calendar lookup and event creation
routine.output:
proposed exhibition
mina's glasswork at larch quay gallery
all day: 21 november. calendar: personal.
no guests, guest emails or meeting link.
add this event?

steps: connect google calendar with read and write access for this bot.
name the calendar and time zone. ask it to list calendars if the name is unclear.
try one event. choose guest emails and meeting-link options, then ask to review before creation.
open the saved event in google calendar. pause the routine if it proposes unconfirmed dates.
watch: **find a free slot first.** event creation won't look for clashes; request an availability lookup.
**defaults can surprise guests.** updates default to all attendees; eligible events request a meet link.
**no time zone means utc.** spell yours out, especially for repeating events.
**your laptop must stay awake.** missed runs under 12 hours old run once on return. older runs skip. dusk cloud runs on time.

faq.q: can i ask for a whole-day event instead of choosing hours?
faq.a: **yes. give dates rather than hours.** the end date falls outside the event. for one day, the bot uses the next date as the end.

faq.q: will it warn me if i already have a meeting?
faq.a: **ask for an availability lookup before creating it.** event creation alone won't warn you about a clash.

faq.q: does adding a guest send an invitation email?
faq.a: **by default, yes.** google emails all attendees. dusk counts event creation as a change. put review and notification choices directly in your request.

steps: name a calendar and your time zone
ask for a ten-minute test event with no guests
request no meet link and no guest emails
review the proposal before it creates anything

mistakes.fix: give the date, time zone and duration. ambiguity costs calendar space.

mistakes.mistake: expecting sending approval to catch guest emails
mistakes.fix: event creation is a change. ask to review before creation.

tip.text: ask for the calendar name, local time and guest list together before booking.

all-day dates cover the intended days
guest emails and meeting links match your choice
